title: Choose the visual world for brickbot.ro (round 4)
question: Back to the people: every card is built on photographs of the students, with this season's results as facts beside them, never as a boast. The roll assigned On Tour.

options.label: On Tour
options.lineage: band tour photobooks, tour-shirt date lists and backstage laminates
options.thesis: The season as a tour: candid photos of the students on the road, the stops listed like a tour shirt's dates, and partners get the all-access pass.
materials: white-bordered photobook prints, stacked with real depth
yellow laminate pass on a burgundy lanyard
options.viewport: Left: 'On tour with BrickBot 2025–26' and the stops as a plain date list (East League, Nationals, FIRST Championship, Twin Cup, schools in Focșani every week). Right: three big candid prints overlap — the celebration, the drive team, a classroom — and a yellow 'All access' laminate hangs in, its link going to partnering.
options.risk: Band-tour styling can look like music merch; the photos must carry it, with the props kept few and real.

raised.raise: Each stop's result sits in measured tabular figures in its row, stated plainly as fact.
Photos open from where they sit: a print grows into the lightbox from its own position.
The stops form a real, semantic table underneath the styling.
Display type fills its column edge to edge, at full scale.

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: photojournalists' contact sheets, grease pencil and loupe
options.thesis: The season as a photographer's contact sheet: dozens of real frames of the students, with the keepers circled in brand-yellow grease pencil and a loupe that enlarges them.
options.viewport: 'Thirty teenagers. One robot. A season worth keeping.' beside a sheet of twelve frames from the season; the keeper is circled in yellow and enlarged under a loupe.
options.risk: Familiar: contact sheets are a well-known editorial device, and the small frames hurt on phones unless the loupe does the work.

options.label: Annotated Spread
options.lineage: Japanese fashion-mook spreads with hand-drawn annotation ribbons
options.thesis: Shingled photos of the students, each annotated by hand with what they actually do: first season in CAD, drive coach, Nationals in March.
options.viewport: Four overlapping photos fill the screen with yellow ribbon annotations curling out to roles and moments; below them, 'Who they were in September. Who they are now.'
options.case: The strongest card on impact on young people: it shows the roles and the growth. Weaker for sponsors, who need the performance more visible.
options.risk: Handwriting can get cute; the notes must be few, true, and written in the team's voice.

options.label: Yellow Hall
options.lineage: an indoor sun installation: one light, a hall full of people
options.thesis: The brand yellow as one great light, with the whole team and the kids they reach gathered in it.
materials: photographs set in black against the light
options.viewport: A yellow screen with a half sun; the celebration photo spans the lower half in black ink against the light; a short headline and one quiet action sit above it.
options.case: Bold and warm, with people at the centre. Faces flatten in the duotone, which costs individual students their detail.
options.risk: Drenched yellow is intense, and the duotone can lose faces.

options.label: Fight Poster
options.thesis: Two names colliding at a versus mark.
options.case: Declined: 'versus' is rivalry, which goes against FIRST's values, and it's close to the bill you passed on.
options.kept: Type that fills its column edge to edge.

options.label: Forge
options.viewport: A glowing bar under the hammer.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.case: Declined: a retro-computing costume that turns photos into dither.
options.kept: Photos open from where they sit.

options.label: Split-flap Board
options.case: Declined: too close to the Destination Blind, and there are no people in it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark team site with a yellow accent, built to the level of team254.com and citruscircuits.org.
canonCard.viewport: The team photo with a headline and two buttons, then the season, posts and sponsors.
canonCard.risk: Close to the removed first attempt; it looks like every other strong team's site.
